- last30days:last30days: Research what people actually say about any topic in the last 30 days. Pulls posts and engagement from Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web. Includes a doctor health check to diagnose broken or missing sources.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text: Confirmed. Both call sites use `findActive()` purely as a gate, discarding the result, then feed `qbUserId` into `QuickBooksClient.create()`.
Confirmed: `QuickBooksClient.create(userId)` reads from `userIntegrations` (legacy, user-scoped), entirely separate from the `qb_connections` table gated by `findActive`.

1	import 'server-only';
2	import { db, type withTransaction } from '@/lib/db';
3	import { accountingProviderConnections, qbConnections } from '@/lib/schema';
4	import type {
5	  QbConnection,
6	  UpdateTokensInput,
7	  UpsertQbConnectionInput,
8	} from '@/types/quickbooks';
9	import { QBNotConnectedError } from '@/types/quickbooks';
10	import { and, eq, inArray, lte } from 'drizzle-orm';
11	
12	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
13	// Transaction type — mirrors the pattern in mvp-v2.repository.impl.ts
14	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
15	
16	type DbTx = Parameters<Parameters<typeof withTransaction>[0]>[0];
17	
18	const USABLE_QB_CONNECTION_STATUSES = ['active', 'refresh_expiring_soon'];
19	
20	function isMissingAccountingProviderTableError(error: unknown): boolean {
21	  const maybeError = error as { code?: unknown; message?: unknown };
22	  // Postgres undefined_table code for missing relation.
23	  if (maybeError?.code === '42P01') return true;
24	
25	  const message =
26	    typeof maybeError?.message === 'string'
27	      ? maybeError.message
28	      : error instanceof Error
29	        ? error.message
30	        : '';
31	
32	  return /relation\s+["']?accounting_provider_connections["']?\s+does not exist/i.test(
33	    message,
34	  );
35	}
36	
37	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
38	// Queries
39	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
40	
41	/**
42	 * Returns a usable QB connection for the given flight school.
43	 * Throws QBNotConnectedError if no row exists or status is not usable.
44	 *
45	 * Use this in every service that needs to make a QB API call.
46	 */
47	export async function findActive(
48	  flightSchoolId: string,
49	  tx?: DbTx,
50	): Promise<QbConnection> {
51	  const client = tx ?? db;
52	  const [row] = await client
53	    .select()
54	    .from(qbConnections)
55	    .where(
56	      and(
57	        eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId),
58	        inArray(qbConnections.status, USABLE_QB_CONNECTION_STATUSES),
59	      ),
60	    )
61	    .limit(1);
62	
63	  if (!row) {
64	    throw new QBNotConnectedError(flightSchoolId);
65	  }
66	
67	  return row;
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Returns the QB connection row for status display, including disconnected,
72	 * token_expired, error, and refresh_expiring_soon states.
73	 */
74	export async function findBySchool(
75	  flightSchoolId: string,
76	  tx?: DbTx,
77	): Promise<QbConnection | null> {
78	  const client = tx ?? db;
79	  const [row] = await client
80	    .select()
81	    .from(qbConnections)
82	    .where(eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId))
83	    .limit(1);
84	
85	  return row ?? null;
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * Returns all flight schools with active QB connections.
90	 *
91	 * INTENTIONALLY CROSS-SCHOOL — used exclusively by the CDC cron job
92	 * (/api/cron/qb-cdc) to iterate all schools. Never use in request handlers.
93	 */
94	export async function findAllActive(tx?: DbTx): Promise<QbConnection[]> {
95	  const client = tx ?? db;
96	  return client
97	    .select()
98	    .from(qbConnections)
99	    .where(eq(qbConnections.status, 'active'));
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * Looks up a connection by QB realmId (QB company ID).
104	 * Used by the webhook handler to route an inbound event to the correct school.
105	 *
106	 * NOTE: This query is intentionally unscoped by flightSchoolId — the caller
107	 * only has the realmId from the webhook payload. The returned row includes
108	 * flightSchoolId which the caller must use for all subsequent scoped queries.
109	 */
110	export async function findByRealmId(
111	  realmId: string,
112	  tx?: DbTx,
113	): Promise<QbConnection | null> {
114	  const client = tx ?? db;
115	  const [row] = await client
116	    .select()
117	    .from(qbConnections)
118	    .where(eq(qbConnections.realmId, realmId))
119	    .limit(1);
120	
121	  return row ?? null;
122	}
123	
124	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
125	// Writes
126	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
127	
128	/**
129	 * Insert or update the QB connection for a flight school.
130	 * On conflict (flightSchoolId), updates all mutable token fields.
131	 * Called by the OAuth callback route after token exchange.
132	 */
133	export async function upsertConnection(
134	  data: UpsertQbConnectionInput,
135	  tx?: DbTx,
136	): Promise<QbConnection> {
137	  const client = tx ?? db;
138	  const now = new Date();
139	
140	  const [row] = await client
141	    .insert(qbConnections)
142	    .values({
143	      flightSchoolId: data.flightSchoolId,
144	      realmId: data.realmId,
145	      accessTokenEncrypted: data.accessTokenEncrypted,
146	      refreshTokenEncrypted: data.refreshTokenEncrypted,
147	      tokenExpiresAt: data.tokenExpiresAt,
148	      refreshTokenExpiresAt: data.refreshTokenExpiresAt,
149	      status: data.status ?? 'active',
150	      connectedAt: now,
151	      updatedAt: now,
152	    })
153	    .onConflictDoUpdate({
154	      target: qbConnections.flightSchoolId,
155	      set: {
156	        realmId: data.realmId,
157	        accessTokenEncrypted: data.accessTokenEncrypted,
158	        refreshTokenEncrypted: data.refreshTokenEncrypted,
159	        tokenExpiresAt: data.tokenExpiresAt,
160	        refreshTokenExpiresAt: data.refreshTokenExpiresAt,
161	        status: data.status ?? 'active',
162	        connectedAt: now,
163	        disconnectedAt: null,
164	        updatedAt: now,
165	      },
166	    })
167	    .returning();
168	
169	  return row;
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Update access/refresh tokens after a proactive token refresh.
174	 * Always scoped to flightSchoolId.
175	 */
176	export async function updateTokens(
177	  flightSchoolId: string,
178	  data: UpdateTokensInput,
179	  tx?: DbTx,
180	): Promise<void> {
181	  const client = tx ?? db;
182	  const now = new Date();
183	  await client
184	    .update(qbConnections)
185	    .set({
186	      accessTokenEncrypted: data.accessTokenEncrypted,
187	      refreshTokenEncrypted: data.refreshTokenEncrypted,
188	      tokenExpiresAt: data.tokenExpiresAt,
189	      ...(data.refreshTokenExpiresAt
190	        ? { refreshTokenExpiresAt: data.refreshTokenExpiresAt }
191	        : {}),
192	      status: 'active',
193	      updatedAt: now,
194	    })
195	    .where(eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId));
196	
197	  try {
198	    await client
199	      .update(accountingProviderConnections)
200	      .set({
201	        oauthAccessTokenEncrypted: data.accessTokenEncrypted,
202	        oauthRefreshTokenEncrypted: data.refreshTokenEncrypted,
203	        oauthAccessTokenExpiresAt: data.tokenExpiresAt,
204	        ...(data.refreshTokenExpiresAt
205	          ? { oauthRefreshTokenExpiresAt: data.refreshTokenExpiresAt }
206	          : {}),
207	        lastOAuthRefreshAt: now,
208	        reconnectRequiredAt: null,
209	        status: 'active',
210	        updatedAt: now,
211	      })
212	      .where(
213	        and(
214	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.ownerType, 'FLIGHT_SCHOOL'),
215	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.ownerId, flightSchoolId),
216	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.provider, 'QUICKBOOKS'),
217	        ),
218	      );
219	  } catch (error) {
220	    if (!isMissingAccountingProviderTableError(error)) throw error;
221	  }
222	}
223	
224	/**
225	 * Stamp the last successful CDC sync timestamp for the school.
226	 * Called at the end of each CDC cron iteration.
227	 */
228	export async function updateCdcSyncAt(
229	  flightSchoolId: string,
230	  syncedAt: Date,
231	  tx?: DbTx,
232	): Promise<void> {
233	  const client = tx ?? db;
234	  await client
235	    .update(qbConnections)
236	    .set({ lastCdcSyncAt: syncedAt, updatedAt: new Date() })
237	    .where(eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId));
238	}
239	
240	/**
241	 * Set the connection status for a flight school.
242	 * Use for 'active' | 'disconnected' | 'token_expired' | 'error' | 'refresh_expiring_soon'.
243	 */
244	export async function setStatus(
245	  flightSchoolId: string,
246	  status: string,
247	  tx?: DbTx,
248	): Promise<void> {
249	  const client = tx ?? db;
250	  await client
251	    .update(qbConnections)
252	    .set({ status, updatedAt: new Date() })
253	    .where(eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId));
254	}
255	
256	export async function markReconnectRequired(
257	  flightSchoolId: string,
258	  reason: 'token_expired' | 'reconnect_required' | 'permission_required',
259	  tx?: DbTx,
260	): Promise<void> {
261	  const client = tx ?? db;
262	  const now = new Date();
263	  const qbStatus = reason === 'permission_required' ? 'error' : 'token_expired';
264	  const providerStatus =
265	    reason === 'permission_required'
266	      ? 'permission_required'
267	      : 'reconnect_required';
268	
269	  await client
270	    .update(qbConnections)
271	    .set({ status: qbStatus, updatedAt: now })
272	    .where(eq(qbConnections.flightSchoolId, flightSchoolId));
273	
274	  try {
275	    await client
276	      .update(accountingProviderConnections)
277	      .set({
278	        status: providerStatus,
279	        reconnectRequiredAt: now,
280	        updatedAt: now,
281	      })
282	      .where(
283	        and(
284	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.ownerType, 'FLIGHT_SCHOOL'),
285	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.ownerId, flightSchoolId),
286	          eq(accountingProviderConnections.provider, 'QUICKBOOKS'),
287	        ),
288	      );
289	  } catch (error) {
290	    if (!isMissingAccountingProviderTableError(error)) throw error;
